businessContext: This crate compiles a slice of the Rigorix engine to WebAssembly so that a host application (a browser demo today, a partner product later) can run the real gate locally: evaluate whether an AI agent's proposed action may proceed, refuse it with evidence when it may not, produce signed envelopes, and verify them offline. The engine already owns the domains; this crate owns the seam, the adapters and the guarantee that its output is byte-identical to the CLI's for the same input. WHAT THIS CRATE OWNS - a portable session: load a scenario from the engine's existing template and sequence-policy formats, plus a host-supplied business world (fixtures). - the adapter ports and their no-I/O implementations: clock, key source, provider transport (fixture-driven, no network), business sink (what a step would have written), randomness. - the host contract: attempt an action, receive an outcome (allowed, or refused with a business-worded reason and an evidence reference), export the artifact set, verify it. - the conformance guarantee against the shipped CLI. WHAT IT DOES NOT OWN (borrowed from rigorix-engine, never re-modeled) - precondition evaluation, sequence/requirement policy evaluation, approval binding, envelope construction and signing, identity attestation, the verifier. - the business domain: no cost sheet, no quote, no ledger semantics live here. ACTORS AND SYSTEMS - the host app: owns the UI and the mock business system; supplies fixtures. - the engine: owns the decision logic and the artifact format. - the approver (human) and the auditor/recipient who verifies a record without trusting the producer. - the CLI: the reference runtime. Same scenario, same artifacts, byte for byte. INVARIANTS THE EXPLORATION MUST ENCODE - Determinism: same scenario + same fixture answers + same clock input produce the same envelopes. Time and randomness are ports, never ambient. - The host cannot influence a decision. Anything a host supplies is data the policy evaluates, never authority. - Fail closed: a port that fails or is missing yields a refusal, never an allow. - No secrets, no absolute host paths, no personal data in artifacts. - An artifact produced in the browser verifies under the independent SDK (rigorix-verifier), which shares no code with this crate. QUESTIONS TO ANSWER - Which bounded contexts exist here, if any, and which concepts are value objects (attempt identity, scenario reference, evidence reference, outcome)? - What is the aggregate, if there is one, and what are its invariants? - Which domain events are produced, and are they evidence or telemetry? - Where exactly is the trust boundary between host, crate and engine, and what crosses it in each direction? - How is a port failure represented so the refusal vocabulary matches the engine's (an unverified session must not read as unauthenticated)? - What is the module decomposition, with the reason each module exists and the invariant it protects? - How is the CLI/WASM conformance property tested, including a seeded divergence that must fail the build? NON-GOALS - running shell commands, network calls, or filesystem access in the browser; - reimplementing any engine logic in JavaScript or TypeScript; - providing a server, an API, or persistence; - being the source of truth for gate behaviour (the engine is). ENVIRONMENT - target wasm32-unknown-unknown, no filesystem, no network, single-threaded; - size budget for the bundle, enforced in CI; - engine changes may only be additive behind non-default features, so the four published crates (engine, mcp, cli, actions) behave exactly as released; - the crate ships in the release train and publishes an npm package at the same version as the engine. , check other crates, architecture docs located in -pi to have a full picture

actors.name: Host application
actors.description: Browser demo today, partner product later; owns UI, mock business system and fixture supply.
actors.interactions: Calls the host contract: load scenario, submit attempt, export artifact set, request verification. Supplies only data (fixtures, clock input, randomness seed), never authority.

actors.name: Rigorix engine (rigorix-engine)
actors.description: Owner of the gate: precondition and sequence/requirement policy evaluation, approval binding, envelope construction/signing, identity attestation.
actors.interactions: Consumed through additive, non-default features; never re-modeled. Returns findings, verdicts, envelopes, evidence references.

actors.name: CLI reference runtime
actors.description: The shipped rigorix CLI; the conformance oracle.
actors.interactions: Produces golden artifact vectors for the same scenario, fixtures and clock; divergence fails the build.

actors.name: Approver (human)
actors.description: The person whose decision the gate consults; their decision is an input fact, not a host capability.
actors.interactions: Approval is expressed as fixture/approval-binding data evaluated by the engine; the crate never grants approval.

actors.name: Auditor / recipient
actors.description: Verifies an exported record offline without trusting producer or host.
actors.interactions: Uses the independent rigorix-verifier SDK on the exported artifact set; result is record-verified or not, never 'trusted'.

assumptions.assumption: The engine can be compiled to wasm32-unknown-unknown behind additive, non-default features, with no filesystem, network or thread dependency on the exercised paths.
assumptions.impactIfWrong: The crate cannot reuse engine logic and would be forced to duplicate it, breaking the source-of-truth invariant.
assumptions.mitigation: Feature-gated seam in the engine; a CI job builds the wasm target with default features of the four published crates unchanged; refuse to ship if any engine change touches a default path.

assumptions.assumption: Every source of nondeterminism (time, identifiers, keys, randomness, provider answers, business world) can be enumerated as an explicit port and captured in a typed fixture transcript. Measured today: 292 Utc::now() call sites, 37 Uuid::new_v4() in the gate modules, and no Clock trait in the engine.
assumptions.impactIfWrong: Browser and CLI envelopes diverge and determinism cannot be asserted or replayed.
assumptions.mitigation: Ports are the only ambient-capability access points, enforced by lint/architecture test; fixture transcripts are versioned and replayed in conformance vectors.

assumptions.assumption: Byte-identical output across native and wasm is achievable with canonical serialization (stable map ordering, fixed field order, fixed hashing/encoding).
assumptions.impactIfWrong: The conformance guarantee degrades to semantically-equal, and the whole value proposition of 'same artifacts' fails.
assumptions.mitigation: Canonical serialization owned by the engine; golden byte vectors checked per release; indexmap/ordered structure use audited.

assumptions.assumption: The verifier (rigorix-verifier) publishes at the same version and can verify browser-produced artifacts with no shared code.
assumptions.impactIfWrong: The 'verifies offline under an independent SDK' invariant is untestable.
assumptions.mitigation: Release train couples versions; CI runs the verifier against freshly exported browser artifacts on every release candidate.

assumptions.assumption: A host cannot influence a decision through any input it supplies — fixtures are evaluated, not trusted.
assumptions.impactIfWrong: The gate becomes host-controlled, invalidating the audit record.
assumptions.mitigation: Single attempt path with no host-settable verdict; any port failure maps to a refusal; a seeded 'host says allow' divergence test must fail the build.

assumptions.assumption: The CLI can be given the same pinned clock and id sequence as the seam.
assumptions.impactIfWrong: Byte-identical conformance is impossible, the central claim of the crate degrades to 'semantically equal', and the demo would be showing two different artifacts.
assumptions.mitigation: FR-011 (Clock + IdSource seam reachable from the CLI). Measured false today — there is no such input on the CLI — so FR-007 stays blocked until it lands, and the comparison is never quietly normalised to hide it.

boundedContexts.name: Portable Session
boundedContexts.description: The determinism seam: one run lifecycle bound to an engine scenario reference, a host-supplied fixture world and explicit port readings, replayable to identical artifact bytes. This is the only domain the crate owns. Modules it decomposes into: domain / application / interfaces (the published host contract and the wasm-bindgen surface) / infrastructure (the five deterministic adapters and the verifier bridge). Conformance is a build-time harness, not a context.
boundedContexts.subdomainRationale: The replayable, byte-identical gate is the crate's reason to exist and the only place it makes a decision; everything else composes engine logic behind ports. It is core rather than supporting because its correctness — determinism, evidence integrity, three-valued verification — is exactly what a host sells.

invariants.rule: No ambient capability on the run path: time, entropy, network and filesystem are reachable only through the five ports.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Two runs of the same session produce different artifact bytes, so a replay cannot be audited or reproduced.

invariants.rule: Every port answer is read from the session's fixture transcript; missing, exhausted, malformed or failed yields a typed PortFailure that becomes a refusal.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: An unanswered port defaults to allow, and an unavailable check is indistinguishable from a passed one.

invariants.rule: The host supplies data evaluated by engine policy, never authority: no API, flag or fixture key can express 'allow' or suppress a finding.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: The gate becomes host-controlled and the record stops being evidence of anything.

invariants.rule: One run per session, sealed at completion with its evidence; neither the outcome nor the artifact set can be reopened or rescored.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: An outcome exists without the evidence that produced it, or evidence is edited after the verdict.

invariants.rule: Timestamps, identifiers and randomness come only from pinned clock readings, the declared id sequence and the declared seed.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Nondeterminism enters through a clock read or a fresh UUID, and conformance with the CLI becomes untestable.

invariants.rule: The crate never issues a verification verdict: it exports the record and its stamp, and the host checks it with the independent SDK, rendering three values — verified, not_verified (compared and does not match), unverifiable (could not ask). The crate's messages never emit those words, so it cannot collapse one into the other.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: A record the host could not check is reported as tampered, or a tampered record is reported as unchecked.

invariants.rule: Artifacts carry no secrets, no key material, no absolute host paths and no personal data; the key exists only as an opaque reference.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: Key material or a host path leaves in an export that is meant to be shared.

invariants.rule: Every artifact set is stamped with scenario digest, engine version and artifact-format version; an unsupported version is refused rather than guessed.
invariants.illegalStatePrevented: A record whose producer and format are unknown is verified against today's rules and appears sound.

contextMap.note: Consumes the engine's gate, policy evaluation, envelope format and signing. Re-models nothing.
Outbound only, through the bridge. The verifier shares no code with this crate; the artifact format is the whole contract.
The CLI built from the same commit is the oracle for byte-identical artifacts.
The host supplies fixtures and consumes RunOutcome, ArtifactSet and VerificationResult. The contract is versioned.

openQuestions:
**None block module planning.** The five questions from the first draft, decided in review:

1. **Is the engine's wasm-facing slice reachable today?** No. Measured: no `cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")`, no wasm-bindgen, and the dependency graph contains blockers (`tree-sitter*`, `reqwest`, `prometheus`, `tracing-appender`, `libc`, and `ring` on the identity path). The seam defines an additive, non-default `portable` feature that swaps the adapters and drops the blockers for that target. Guard: the four published crates build and test unchanged from the same commit, and `cargo tree -e normal,no-dev --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` is diffed before and after.
2. **Does the seam surface an "unverified" state the host could misread?** Yes, and it must: three values (`verified`, `not_verified`, `unverifiable(reason)`), never a boolean. This is the #472/#1285 rule — `false` accuses, `null` reports a question that could not be asked — and FR-006 plus the invariant list make collapsing them a defect.
3. **Live CLI or committed goldens, and who re-baselines?** Both, doing different jobs: CI builds the CLI from the same commit and diffs live (authoritative, catches drift the day it lands); committed golden vectors serve the wasm-side test and the demo build, and are regenerated by that same job so a stale golden fails the live diff rather than waiting for a human. Re-baselining is a generated commit, reviewed like any artifact.
4. **What is the bundle size budget, and what is excluded?** Measured first, then `+25%` as the hard gate (NFR-002). Excluded by necessity: `tree-sitter*`, `reqwest`, `prometheus`, `tracing-appender`, `libc`; `ring` only if it turns out to sit exclusively on the identity/TLS path, verified with `cargo tree --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`. `wasm-opt` in the release build; `wasm-bindgen-cli` pinned to the crate version.
5. **Is approval binding expressible as fixture data?** The decision is data; the act is not this crate's job. The host supplies an approval *claim*; the engine binds it to the intent hash and refuses a mismatch (FR-013). The crate never grants an approval and models no human UI.

Tracked items, each with an exit condition (they do not block module planning):

- **The clock/id seam's call-site inventory** — FR-011 must name every site in the gate path that reads time or mints an id, and prove the published crates are unchanged. Exit: the inventory is a fixed list and the four crates' default-feature suites are green from the same commit.
- **`ring`'s reachability** — whether it is only on the identity/TLS path. Exit: `cargo tree` for the wasm target shows no `ring`, or the identity port is fixture-only and the dependency is provably unreachable.
- **Key ownership in the browser demo** — a visitor-generated key means the signature proves integrity and binding, not third-party non-repudiation. Exit: the demo's limits panel states it in one sentence, and the artifact stamp records which key produced the record.

**Decided in review (2026-11-03), and now binding:**

- **Who verifies — the host.** ADR-013 removes `VerifyExportedArtifacts` from the crate and `VerifierBridge` from infrastructure. The crate produces; the host checks with the independent SDK, in a process that never loads the wasm module. The independence claim becomes provable: the bundle's dependency tree contains no verifier.
- **The session-store port does not exist.** ADR-002 point 3 is withdrawn: verification's input is the `ArtifactSet`, not a session. A store port would exist only to persist a live aggregate and would invite a host to treat a stored session as evidence.
- **Failure semantics are tiered, not monolithic.** ADR-012 replaces NFR-004's single promise: refusals are typed and tested; panics are build-time defects (baseline + deny-lints); traps are fatal and host-visible. `catch_unwind` is documented as unavailable, not merely unused.
- **The crate is `rigorix-gate-wasm`, the npm package `rigorix-gate`, version-locked to the train, licence inherited.** ADR-011 adds the six registration points, including the `release.yml` tag loop that `rigorix-actions` fell out of for seven weeks.

functionalRequirements.requirement: The system shall open a Portable Session from an engine scenario reference (existing template and sequence-policy formats) plus a host-supplied fixture world, rejecting any input that does not parse under the engine's own types with a typed refusal rather than a default.

The system shall accept a run request and return exactly one RunOutcome: a status (allowed | refused) plus the ordered StepOutcome list and evidence references. No step may be reported refused at the run level without the step that caused it, and no host-settable verdict shall be expressible.

The system shall satisfy every engine-declared port (clock, key source, provider transport, business sink, randomness) exclusively from the session's fixture transcript, so that no attempt performs a network, filesystem, OS-time or ambient-entropy access.

The system shall map any missing, exhausted, malformed or failed port answer to a typed PortFailure that becomes a refusal expressed in the engine's vocabulary — `unverified` for an identity port that could not be checked, never `unauthenticated` — and shall never map a port failure to an allow.

The system shall export the produced artifact set (envelopes, evidence references, scenario digest) as a self-contained byte sequence containing no secrets, no absolute host paths and no personal data, and shall make that export the only supported input to verification.

The system shall export an artifact set that the host verifies with the independent rigorix-verifier SDK; the crate shall contain no verification logic and shall not depend on a verifier, so the producer cannot ship the checker (ADR-013). The three-valued vocabulary (verified / not_verified / unverifiable) is the host's to render, and the host contract states it.

The system shall produce artifacts byte-identical to a CLI built from the same commit for the same scenario, fixture transcript and pinned clock/seed inputs, and shall fail the build when either the live CLI diff or a committed golden vector diverges. A skipped or missing vector is a failure, never a pass.
The system shall run a seeded divergence vector (a deliberately altered fixture answer or serialization field) as a conformance test that is required to fail; if it passes, the build shall fail.

The system shall treat every host-supplied value (fixtures, approvals, provider answers, business-sink writes) as data evaluated by engine policy, and shall expose no API, flag or fixture key that can force an allow or suppress a finding.

The system shall stamp each exported artifact set with the scenario digest, engine version and artifact-format version, and shall refuse to verify an artifact set whose format/version it does not support rather than guessing.

Deterministic inputs shall be supplied by the engine, not invented by this crate: an additive Clock and IdSource seam covering the gate path, defaulting to system time and reachable from the CLI behind a non-default feature. A feasibility spike precedes the crate: the engine's gate slice must compile to wasm32-unknown-unknown and one envelope's bytes must match the CLI's before Phase 0 begins. FR-007 is blocked until the seam lands; a normalised comparison is a label on a failing claim, never a pass.

Conformance shall never compare approximately. A field that is nondeterministic must be pinned by FR-011, not normalised away before comparison; a normalised comparison is permitted only as a labelled interim and must be deleted, not relaxed, when FR-011 lands.
An approval shall enter as a claim the host supplies and the engine evaluates. The crate shall never grant an approval, and shall refuse a claim whose binding does not match the run's intent hash.
Every exported artifact set shall carry the artifact-format version and the engine version, and verification of an unknown format version shall return unverifiable with that reason.

nonFunctionalRequirements.requirement: The system shall be deterministic: repeated runs with identical scenario, fixture transcript and clock input produce identical artifact bytes within a process and across processes.
nonFunctionalRequirements.target: 100% byte equality on the golden vector suite; zero ambient time/entropy/network/fs calls on the attempt path (architecture test fails otherwise)

nonFunctionalRequirements.requirement: The system shall keep the shipped WebAssembly bundle within the release train's size budget, enforced in CI as a hard gate.
nonFunctionalRequirements.target: Budget is set from a measurement, not a guess: the first green build's bundle size + 25%, enforced as a hard CI gate (regressions beyond the budget fail); no tokio runtime, reqwest, tree-sitter, prometheus, tracing-appender or libc in the wasm dependency graph

nonFunctionalRequirements.requirement: The system shall keep secrets, key material, absolute host paths and personal data out of artifacts and out of any error or log message surfaced to the host.
nonFunctionalRequirements.target: Zero findings from a secret/PII/path scanner over exported artifacts and refusal messages in CI; key material exists only as an opaque test-key reference

nonFunctionalRequirements.requirement: The system shall fail closed in three tiers: a logical failure (exhausted/missing/malformed fixture answer, unparseable scenario, unsupported format, unusable port) yields a typed refusal; a panic on the gate path is a defect that must not exist and is caught at build time by the panic-site baseline and deny-lints; a trap is surfaced to the host as fatal and is never rendered as a refusal or an allow (ADR-012).
nonFunctionalRequirements.target: 100% of tier-1 injected faults return a typed refusal with zero allows; zero unclassed panic sites on the gate path; a host-contract test asserts a trap is fatal, distinct from refused

nonFunctionalRequirements.requirement: The system shall require engine changes to be additive and behind non-default features, leaving the four published crates (engine, mcp, cli, actions) behaviourally unchanged, and shall publish at the engine's version.
nonFunctionalRequirements.target: Default-feature test suites of all four crates green and unchanged per release; wasm npm package version strictly equal to rigorix-engine version

applicationServices.name: OpenReplaySession
applicationServices.useCase: Assemble a replayable session from an engine scenario reference and a host fixture transcript: parse with engine types, pin the clock series and seed, and reject anything incomplete with a typed refusal.
applicationServices.commands: load scenario reference,validate fixture transcript,pin clock readings and random seed,bind attempt identity

applicationServices.name: AttemptRun
applicationServices.useCase: Drive one attempt through the engine's gate: resolve every port answer from the transcript, hand the run to engine policy evaluation, and project the RunOutcome with its ordered StepOutcomes and evidence references. A missing or failed port answer becomes a refusal, never an allow.
applicationServices.commands: resolve port answers,invoke engine evaluation,project run outcome,record port failure as refusal

applicationServices.name: ExportArtifactSet
applicationServices.useCase: Serialize the sealed envelopes and evidence references into a self-contained artifact set, stamped with scenario digest, engine version and format version, scanned for secrets, absolute paths and personal data before it leaves — and handed to the host, which verifies it (ADR-013).
applicationServices.commands: collect envelopes and evidence refs,stamp scenario/engine/format versions,scan and reject forbidden content,emit artifact bytes

applicationServices.name: RunConformanceVector
applicationServices.useCase: Replay a versioned scenario/fixture/clock vector through the wasm seam and through a CLI built from the same commit, compare artifacts byte for byte, and fail the build on any divergence or on a seeded divergence that does not diverge.
applicationServices.commands: load golden vector,build CLI from same commit,replay both,compare bytes,assert seeded divergence fails

domainEvents.name: ReplaySessionOpened
domainEvents.description: A session was accepted with a scenario digest, fixture-transcript digest, pinned clock series and random seed — the replay key.

domainEvents.name: RunAllowed
domainEvents.description: The engine's gate permitted every step of the run; carries the evidence references and the approved action digests.

domainEvents.name: RunRefused
domainEvents.description: The run did not proceed; carries the step that caused it, a business-worded reason and an EvidenceRef.

domainEvents.name: StepDecisionRecorded
domainEvents.description: One gated step's decision was recorded inside the run — allowed, refused, or not reached.

domainEvents.name: PortAnswerUnavailable
domainEvents.description: A port could not answer for this attempt; recorded as evidence of why the gate refused and as the fixture author's signal.

domainEvents.name: RandomDrawConsumed
domainEvents.description: A randomness answer was drawn from the seeded sequence at a declared index.

domainEvents.name: ArtifactSetExported
domainEvents.description: The sealed artifact set was exported, stamped with scenario digest, engine version and format version.

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: The replayable unit: one scenario reference, one fixture world, one clock-reading series and one random seed, enclosing at most one attempt.
ubiquitousLanguage.aliases: Attempt Session, session, run, playground session

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: One proposed run submitted to the gate, identified by GateAttemptId; its outcome is not a business approval.
The result of one attempt: status plus the ordered StepOutcome list and the evidence references. No third shape, no host-settable verdict.
The decision for one gated step: allowed, refused or not reached, with the engine's gate id and reason.
A digest-bearing pointer to an engine scenario in the engine's own template and sequence-policy formats, never a re-typed policy.
The host-supplied immutable transcript of answers a port may give; data the policy evaluates, never authority.
ubiquitousLanguage.aliases: mock data, test data, stub, fixture blob

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: A port's inability to answer — missing, exhausted, malformed or failed — which forces a refusal. For the identity port the engine's truthful status is `unverified`; a failure is never reported as `unauthenticated`.
A pinned instant answered by the clock port at a declared index; the only source of time in a session.
The declared seed and recorded draw sequence that make randomness replayable.
A stable reference to the facts a record carries (what was checked, when, outcome, digests) — borrowed from the engine, never minted here.
The exported, version-stamped byte sequence: envelopes, evidence references, scenario digest, engine and format versions.
Three-valued verdict on an artifact set: verified, not_verified, or unverifiable with a reason.

entities.name: ReplaySession
entities.description: Aggregate root (identity ReplaySessionId): owns the scenario reference, the fixture-world pin, the pinned clock-reading series, the random seed, at most one GateAttempt, and the sealed ArtifactSet.

entities.name: GateAttempt
entities.description: One proposed run under evaluation (identity GateAttemptId): carries the action and parameters, the resolved port answers and the RunOutcome. Never reopened or rescored, and it is not a business transaction.

entities.name: ScenarioRef
entities.description: Digest-bearing reference to an engine scenario in the engine's own template and sequence-policy formats; equal by digest and declared format version.

entities.name: FixtureWorld
entities.description: Immutable, versioned host-supplied transcript (provider answers, business-sink expectations, approval claims) that the engine evaluates as data; equal by transcript digest.

entities.name: PortFailure
entities.description: Typed record that a port could not answer (missing, exhausted, malformed, failed), carrying the port name and an engine-aligned failure kind; projects to a refusal reason.

entities.name: ClockReading
entities.description: One pinned instant plus its declared ordering index; the session's only source of time.

entities.name: RandomSeed
entities.description: The declared seed and the recorded draw sequence; equal by seed and draw digest, replayable to the same values.

entities.name: RunOutcome
entities.description: The single result of an attempt: status (allowed | refused) plus the ordered StepOutcome list and the evidence references. There is no host-settable verdict and no run-level refusal without the step that caused it.

entities.name: StepOutcome
entities.description: Per gated step: step name, decision (allowed | refused | not_reached), the engine's refusal kind and gate id, a business-worded reason, and the EvidenceRef it produced.

entities.name: EvidenceRef
entities.description: Stable reference to the facts a record carries — what was checked, when, with what outcome, which digests bind it. Borrowed from the engine, never minted here.

entities.name: ArtifactSet
entities.description: The exported byte sequence: produced envelopes, evidence references, scenario digest, engine version and artifact-format version.

entities.name: VerificationResult
entities.description: Three-valued: verified | not_verified | unverifiable(reason). Reason is populated only for unverifiable (unsupported format version, absent key, key not held).
